name: Expertise-Gated Aesthetic Processing Circuit
short_description: Gates depth of aesthetic processing based on expertise level and perceptual fluency, allowing novices and experts to engage aesthetic objects at appropriate levels of complexity.

components.name: EXPERTISE_GATE
components.description: Opens or closes aesthetic processing pathways based on domain expertise

components.name: COMPLEXITY_PROCESSOR
components.description: Processes stimulus complexity, depth of features, and stylistic details

components.name: FLUENCY_INTEGRATOR
components.description: Combines perceptual fluency with expertise gate to determine processing depth

components.name: APPRECIATION_INTEGRATOR
components.description: Generates aesthetic appreciation based on appropriately-gated complexity processing

key_references: Leder, H., Belke, B., Oeberst, A., & Augustin, D. (2004). A model of aesthetic appreciation and aesthetic judgments. British Journal of Psychology, 95(4), 489–508.
Silvia, P. J. (2005). Emotional responses to art: From collation and arousal to cognition and emotion. Review of General Psychology, 9(4), 342–357.
design_implications: Novice and expert audiences appreciate different aspects of complex works; provide layered aesthetic content (surface beauty + conceptual depth) to serve audiences at varying expertise levels
Museums and galleries should scaffold aesthetic learning; begin with accessible perceptual features and gradually reveal complexity to support expertise development
